content: Integrin alpha-9 (ITGA9) is a protein in humans that is encoded by the ITGA9 gene. This gene encodes an alpha integrin, which is a component of integrins—heterodimeric integral membrane glycoproteins. Integrins are composed of an alpha chain and a beta chain, and they play a critical role in mediating cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion. The protein encoded by the ITGA9 gene, when paired with the beta-1 chain, forms an integrin that functions as a receptor for tenascin-C, vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM-1), and osteopontin. Notably, the expression of the ITGA9 gene has been observed to be upregulated in small cell lung cancers. The alpha-9 (α9) subunit associates with the beta-1 (β1) subunit to form the α9β1 integrin heterodimeric complex. This integrin is involved in cell adhesion by interacting with various ligands in the extracellular matrix (ECM), including extra domain A (EDA) fibronectin, tenascin-C, ADAMs (a disintegrin and metalloproteinase family), EMILIN-1 (elastin microfibril interface-located protein 1), osteopontin, and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Importantly, the binding of α9β1 integrin to its ligands does not depend on the RGD (arginine-glycine-aspartic acid) peptide sequence.
